construction_invariant: A lathe-turned solid of revolution made as its OWN part and attached to the member above by a dowel or a square block. The joint is proved, not assumed.
geometry_generator: revolve of a 2D profile (pad / ball or bun / neck / collar)
host_interface: underside of plinth, leg blank or case base
joint_schedule: dowel into plinth (1984.161, stated); square block above the ball seen in the underside view (2019.59); applied under the rear post (2011.3)
assembly_role: floor contact, load path into the case
surface_realization: ebonised, gilt or clear-finished turned wood
permitted_variation: ball/bun/onion/trumpet silhouette; height; max diameter; ring count and pitch; pad diameter and thickness; dowel diameter
incompatible_excluded: every integral turned terminal - attaching one of these would mean CUTTING the leg and changing its joint schedule; every prismatic termination; the spun-metal base
donor_status: AUDIT_REQUIRED - no turned-solid donor located; rough_hewn_timber_beam_v1 is hewn, shares no lathe logic; silhouette/section/joints NOT compared
note: The only foot family where BOTH the revolved geometry and the host interface are source-visible. This is what v2's foot.turned_separate should have been.

construction_invariant: NOT a separate part. The turned terminal is the bottom of the leg or post turning itself - one blank, one lathe setup, no joint at all.
geometry_generator: continuation of the leg's own revolve profile
host_interface: none - continuous stock with the member above
joint_schedule: none; the interface upward is the seat rail or lower rail mortise
assembly_role: floor contact, continuous with the leg
surface_realization: same finish as the leg it terminates
permitted_variation: toe fullness; ring/collar count above the toe; where the taper stops
incompatible_excluded: every dowelled or applied foot - they are a different joint contract entirely
note: Split from the dowelled family on the joint contract, per the v2 audit. 2011.3 carries BOTH constructions on one object, which is why R064 is split.

construction_invariant: Revolved foot geometry is clearly visible; whether it is a separate turning or integral with the member above is NOT resolvable in the published views.
host_interface: UNRESOLVED - the defining open question of this family
joint_schedule: UNRESOLVED
permitted_variation: silhouette; height; diameter; ring count
incompatible_excluded: any row where the interface IS proved, in either direction
note: AUDIT_ONLY - an analysis bucket, never a production queue entry. A visible silhouette with an unknown interface cannot authorise a recipe. R193.a arrives here from foot.turned_integral_with_leg: 69.146.2's post 'transitions into' the turned foot, which describes a shape change, not a proved continuity of stock. 67.230 says so outright: 'Whether the foot is integral to the shaft turning or a separate glued turning is not resolvable from these views.' These rows may not establish a joint.

construction_invariant: Turned foot whose pad is BORED to receive a castor - the socket is part of the recipe.
geometry_generator: revolve, then a bored axial socket
host_interface: leg or post above; castor stem below
joint_schedule: bored socket, castor stem
assembly_role: floor contact via a rolling castor
permitted_variation: height; diameter; ring count above the socket; socket bore
incompatible_excluded: feet with a flat resting face and no castor provision (1999.488 states there are none)
note: One evidenced object. The 4th foot (R322.b) is inferred by symmetry and carries zero weight.

construction_invariant: A flat circular disc pad that seats a carved foot above it and is explicitly reusable on its own.
host_interface: underside of a carved paw/claw master
joint_schedule: glued or dowelled seat under the carved foot
assembly_role: floor contact under a bespoke carving
permitted_variation: diameter; thickness
incompatible_excluded: the carved paw above it, which is bespoke sculpture
note: Extracted from the paw-foot row because the row itself says the pad 'is separable from the paw and reusable alone'. The pad is a recipe; the paw is not.

construction_invariant: A spun or cast metal shell sitting on the plinth - a metal process, not woodturning.
host_interface: top face of the stone plinth
joint_schedule: seated shell, no wood joint
permitted_variation: flare ratio; lappet count round the ring; bead pitch on the upper fillet
incompatible_excluded: all turned-wood feet - different material, process and wall condition
note: Kept separate from wood turning: a spun shell and a solid turning are not one generator even though both are solids of revolution.

construction_invariant: A leg blank ending in a prismatic block, pad flare or chamfer - a cut on the leg, not a solid of revolution and not a separate part.
geometry_generator: prismatic cut / chamfer on the leg blank
host_interface: none - continuous with the leg
joint_schedule: none below; apron or rail mortise above
assembly_role: floor contact at the end of a tapered leg
surface_realization: gilt block, reeded cuff, or plain
permitted_variation: block height; cuff reed count; chamfer angle; pad flare
incompatible_excluded: all revolved feet
note: Per the audit: prismatic integral toes belong in leg-termination logic, not in a foot family. 1969.262 carries an unexplained horizontal seam ~12 cm up which may be an original cuff line or a spliced repair - recorded, not resolved.

construction_invariant: A true structural corner post of a carcase, showing on TWO adjacent faces and mortised on both. Continuity past the case seams is proved by view, not assumed.
geometry_generator: extruded square prism with face treatments
host_interface: case sides and front/back frames on two adjacent faces
joint_schedule: mortise-and-tenon on two ADJACENT faces (this is what separates it from a muntin)
surface_realization: reeded, fluted or ebonised show faces
permitted_variation: height; square section; reed/flute count; roundel diameter at the head; whether the post projects above the cornice
incompatible_excluded: panel muntins (grooved on OPPOSITE faces); applied pilasters (no structural role); posts whose joint schedule is not resolvable
note: 69.140ab is the strongest construction evidence in the corpus: 'confirmed in the rear view where the same black post is unbroken past both case seams.'

construction_invariant: A vertical carcase member whose STRUCTURAL role is not resolvable - it may be a joined corner post or an applied face pilaster.
host_interface: UNRESOLVED
joint_schedule: UNRESOLVED
permitted_variation: height; width; reed count; roundel block count and spacing
incompatible_excluded: posts with a proved joint schedule, in either direction
note: AUDIT_ONLY - a research bucket, not a production recipe. Per the audit: joined structural corner stiles must be split from applied pilasters AND from unresolved carcase posts. These two are the unresolved bucket.

construction_invariant: A decorative strip APPLIED to the face of a carcase post. Carries no load and has no mortise; it masks the post behind it.
host_interface: glued to the face of a post or stile
joint_schedule: glued applique only
permitted_variation: width; profile; length; cross-block count
incompatible_excluded: the structural post underneath, which is a different part with a different joint schedule
note: Extracted from R270 because the row records the applied strip and the post it masks as two separate things.

construction_invariant: An intermediate upright inside a frame, GROOVED ON TWO OPPOSITE FACES to capture the panels either side. Opposite-face grooving is the whole distinction from a corner post.
geometry_generator: extruded prism with a groove on each of two opposite faces
host_interface: upper and lower rails of the frame it divides
joint_schedule: stub tenons into rail mortises; panels float in the grooves, unglued
surface_realization: plain, moulded, or carrying applied spindles
permitted_variation: count (drives bay count); width; section; spacing; whether it carries applied spindles
incompatible_excluded: corner posts, which are mortised on ADJACENT faces; upholstery tacking muntins, which have no groove at all
note: R320 was filed under 'moulding run' in v1 and refiled here in v3; it is QUARANTINED in v3.1 because neither the opposite-face grooves nor the rail tenons are visible - the row records only 'spacing and count across a panel width', which is a layout fact, not a joint schedule.

construction_invariant: An intermediate upright that divides an UPHOLSTERED back into webbing bays. It is a tacking ground - no groove, no panel, and it is invisible when the cover is on.
host_interface: upper and lower back-frame rails
joint_schedule: tenoned or lapped; webbing tacked to its faces
assembly_role: divides an upholstered field into webbing bays
surface_realization: bare secondary wood - never seen in the finished object
permitted_variation: bay count (chair 0, this settee 1, longer sofa 2-3); section
incompatible_excluded: grooved panel muntins - a groove would serve no purpose here
note: The audit's split, and the source supports it exactly: 'central vertical member dividing the upholstered back into two webbing bays; visible only in alt4 with the outer cover off.'

construction_invariant: A SHORT post standing on the seat rail and carrying the arm above it. Both ends are joints; it spans only the seat-to-arm gap.
host_interface: seat rail below, arm rail above
joint_schedule: tenon or dowel at both ends
assembly_role: carries the arm off the seat frame
surface_realization: faceted, gilt, or tapered show wood
permitted_variation: height; taper; section; facet count; carving presence
incompatible_excluded: posts that tie into the BACK frame (different upper host); continuous arm/back stiles (no joint at all)
note: Per the audit, post.arm_support is split three ways by what the post actually connects. This is the short-post-on-seat-rail case.

construction_invariant: A wide FLAT post tying the arm into the back frame. Its upper host is the back frame, not the arm rail, so its joint schedule differs from a short arm post.
host_interface: side seat rail below, back frame behind
joint_schedule: tenon below; lapped or tenoned into the back frame
assembly_role: ties the arm assembly into the back
permitted_variation: width; taper; rake; height
incompatible_excluded: front cone-stump arm posts; continuous arm/back stiles

construction_invariant: One continuous curved member doing arm rail AND back stile AND crest junction with NO joint break. There is nothing to assemble - the modelling error is treating it as parts.
geometry_generator: swept section along a compound 3D curve
host_interface: seat frame below; crest above; both are continuations of the same stick
joint_schedule: NONE along the run - that is the defining fact
assembly_role: arm and back outer edge in one member
surface_realization: gilt show wood, reeded-and-inlaid on the inside face only
permitted_variation: sweep radius; scoop depth under the elbow; section width; whether the inside face carries the reeded band
incompatible_excluded: any jointed arm-post-plus-arm-rail construction
note: 2012.216 states it: 'rises from the front terminal, dips into a shallow scoop under the elbow, and turns up into the back stile WITHOUT A JOINT BREAK.'

construction_invariant: An intermediate vertical in the BACK frame running crest to rear seat rail.
host_interface: crest rail above, rear seat rail below
joint_schedule: tenon at both ends
assembly_role: stiffens a wide back; carries medial rails
permitted_variation: count as a function of back width (1 here; 2-3 for a longer bench); section
incompatible_excluded: arm posts; muntins that capture panels

construction_invariant: A post built as a STACK of discrete solids. Adding or dropping a stage rescales the post without any new geometry - the grammar is the asset, not the post.
host_interface: floor/foot below; tester or finial above
joint_schedule: stacked and pinned; each stage is a separate solid
permitted_variation: stack ORDER and stage count; per-stage height and diameter
incompatible_excluded: one-piece turned or fluted posts
note: 'Each stage is a separate solid; adding or dropping a stage rescales the post without new geometry.'

construction_invariant: One square fluted post recipe run at two different lengths on the same object - the object itself proves length is the parameter.
geometry_generator: extruded square prism, fluted faces, carved capital block
host_interface: floor or corner block below; tester/canopy above
joint_schedule: tenon or dowel at the cap; die block below
surface_realization: gilt on show faces, bare wood on rear faces
permitted_variation: LENGTH (proved: 163.2 cm vs 132.7 cm from one recipe); flute count; flute stop height; capital leaf density; which faces are gilded
incompatible_excluded: stacked-block posts; turned posts
note: The cleanest parametric proof in the corpus: 'the head-end pair and foot-end pair are the SAME square fluted post recipe run at two different lengths.'

construction_invariant: A turned upright that BEARS A PIVOT - the gate swings on it. The bearing is the reason the part exists and it is not shared with any static post.
geometry_generator: revolve with a bored or pinned pivot seat
host_interface: top and bottom rails of the fixed frame
joint_schedule: pivot bearing (pin/socket) top and bottom
assembly_role: hinge axis for a swinging gate leg
permitted_variation: diameter relative to the corner leg; count along the side; presence at all (a 6-leg version drops them)
incompatible_excluded: the stacked stone-and-metal pedestal, which is not a recipe and has no pivot; static turned supports
note: The audit's split of post.turned_support. A pivot-bearing wooden gate post and a stacked alabaster pedestal share only the word 'support'.

construction_invariant: A splayed flat BOARD standard at a trestle end, with applied carving that can be removed to leave a plain trestle.
geometry_generator: tapered flat board, splayed in elevation
host_interface: trestle foot below, top frame above
joint_schedule: tenoned into foot and top rail
surface_realization: carved palmette and swag as APPLIED layers
permitted_variation: height; splay angle; board width; taper
incompatible_excluded: square-section posts; turned supports

construction_invariant: A load-bearing midspan pier under a long carcase, standing on a shelf rather than the floor.
host_interface: shelf below, drawer carcase above
joint_schedule: UNRESOLVED at the shelf; joined by a cross rail to its pair
assembly_role: midspan support for a long span
permitted_variation: pier count along the span (drives arch count); section; height above shelf
incompatible_excluded: trestle standards (which reach the floor)
note: 'whether 2 further piers exist is NOT DETERMINABLE' - the count is open.

construction_invariant: A slender stick supporting a cantilevered shelf and landing on the SHELF BELOW rather than on the carcase - a staggered-shelf grammar.
host_interface: shelf above and shelf below (never the carcase)
joint_schedule: butted/pinned at both ends
permitted_variation: stick section; length; horizontal offset of the shelf it carries
incompatible_excluded: any post that lands on the carcase or the floor
note: 'the single most transferable idea in the object: a staggered shelf held by one thin stick.'

construction_invariant: An interior board partition dividing drawer banks. Its OFFSET sets the bank widths.
host_interface: case top and bottom; drawer runners fix to it
joint_schedule: housed/dadoed into top and bottom; rails tenon into it
assembly_role: divides the interior into drawer banks
permitted_variation: board width (case depth); height; OFFSET from the case end - the single most retargetable parameter in the object
incompatible_excluded: show-face posts and muntins
note: AUDIT_ONLY per the final audit - zero proved construction members. v3 marked this row simultaneously proven and unresolved, which is incoherent. The housing into the case top and bottom is NOT visible in any view; what the row actually establishes is the partition's existence and its offset. Interface UNRESOLVED. (1 of 2 visible, 1 inferred by symmetry - PARTIALLY VISIBLE.)

construction_invariant: One stick doing leg AND stile, unbroken from floor to crest or cornice. Proved by view.
geometry_generator: extruded prism or turning, full height
host_interface: floor below; crest/cornice above
joint_schedule: NONE along the run; rails mortise into it
assembly_role: corner member of the whole object
permitted_variation: total height; section; taper; reed count; where the capital block lands
incompatible_excluded: any object where the rear support is a separate leg under a concealed frame
note: The baseline's defining trait. Note it does NOT hold on 2012.216 or 1954.151 - both explicitly contradict it, and are in the separate-leg family below.

construction_invariant: The rear support is a SEPARATE leg, applied under a seat frame or below a die block. The show-wood stile above stops short and never reaches the floor.
host_interface: seat frame or corner die block above
joint_schedule: dowel or tenon into the frame/die block
surface_realization: may be plain where the front is decorated
permitted_variation: same turning parameters as the front leg; rake angle; whether the rear pair is shortened
incompatible_excluded: continuous leg-and-stile members
note: 1954.151 is emphatic: 'CRITICAL DIVERGENCE FROM THE BASELINE: this is NOT a continuous rear leg-and-stile.' Two objects disprove the baseline pattern.

construction_invariant: A thin board-like corner stile of a case, thinner than the front members - a show-face vs back-face economy rule.
host_interface: case sides and back
joint_schedule: housed or tenoned; rails mortise in
surface_realization: plain or ebonised; deliberately cheaper than the front
permitted_variation: thickness; taper; whether front and rear sections match; whether it stops at a base moulding or runs to the floor
incompatible_excluded: full-section structural corner posts
note: R376 arrives here from the deleted family termination.stile_to_floor. Continuing past the lower rail to the floor is a TERMINATION SETTING on this recipe - the variation axis already reads 'whether it stops at a base moulding or runs to the floor' - not a second component. 1971.281 supplies both the stile (R359) and the proof of the floor setting (R376), so they are one part.

construction_invariant: A plain board closing the back, shaped only by a functional notch. Deliberately undecorated because it is never seen.
host_interface: case sides
joint_schedule: nailed or housed
assembly_role: closes the back; provides floor bearing at the rear
permitted_variation: board width; notch depth and shape
incompatible_excluded: show-face stiles
note: 'deliberately plain because the rear is unseen, in direct contrast to the turned front feet' - the visibility-economy rule stated outright.

construction_invariant: A rear member that LOOKS continuous but whose junction is masked. Continuity is the baseline's defining trait and here it is asserted, not seen.
geometry_generator: prism above, turning below - alignment visible, junction not
host_interface: UNRESOLVED
joint_schedule: UNRESOLVED - masked by the seat rail and gilding
surface_realization: gilt with a recessed matte field
permitted_variation: rake angle; length below seat; recessed field dimensions
incompatible_excluded: members where continuity is proved either way
note: AUDIT_ONLY. THE BASELINE OBJECT'S OWN defining trait is unproven on the baseline object: 'continuity is asserted only as plausible, not seen.'

construction_invariant: A closed rectangle of four rails that must exist for a seat to be framed. This is the OWNERSHIP rule that says the individual rail recipes below compose into one frame - it is not itself a part to model.
host_interface: leg or post at each corner
joint_schedule: tenon, pin or mitre at four corners - varies by member family
assembly_role: the seat frame as a unit
surface_realization: n/a - the members carry the surface
permitted_variation: plan aspect; rail depth; straight vs shaped vs barrel plan
incompatible_excluded: n/a
note: Per the audit, rail.seat_frame is an assembly grammar, and the leaf recipes (show face / secondary / mitred / pinned) are separate families below.

construction_invariant: The tenoned seat rail. ONE recipe: front, side and rear are the same member with the same joint, differing only in which faces get a finish and how deep the rail runs.
geometry_generator: extruded rectangular section, optionally scalloped on the lower edge
host_interface: legs or posts at each corner
joint_schedule: tenoned into posts and leg blocks
assembly_role: front / side / rear leaf of a closed seat frame - the ROLE lives in the assembly schedule, not in a separate recipe
surface_realization: SURFACE IS A PARAMETER: gilt show face with paterae and a bead arris, or bare secondary wood, or upholstered over
permitted_variation: length; depth (deeper where the cover wraps over it); scalloped vs straight lower edge; paterae pitch; PER-FACE finish flag; role (front/side/rear)
incompatible_excluded: pinned/pegged rails, which are a different joint schedule; mitred box rails, which have no tenon at all
note: MERGED in v3.1. v3 split these into rail.seat_show_face and rail.seat_secondary_concealed, but that split is FINISH, not construction - the geometry and the tenon are identical and 2011.3 proves it by carrying both states on one frame ('Front and side rails are gilt show faces carrying paterae; the rear rail is left in bare wood'). Decoration is a per-face flag, which is a parameter.

construction_invariant: A seat rail whose joints are PINNED with visible round pegs - a different joint schedule from a glued tenon, and visible on the finished object.
host_interface: legs or posts at each corner
joint_schedule: tenoned AND PINNED with visible round pegs through the joint
assembly_role: leaf of a closed seat frame
surface_realization: plain secondary wood; the pegs read on the show face
permitted_variation: length; depth; peg count and position; straight vs serpentine front edge in plan
incompatible_excluded: glued tenoned rails - the peg array is real geometry and changes the joint contract
note: Split from the merged tenoned recipe per the audit: 'joints pinned with visible round pegs' is a different joint schedule AND a visible surface event.

construction_invariant: Four flat boards MITRED into a closed rectangular box with no separate apron member. The mitre is the joint contract and it excludes tenoning.
geometry_generator: flat board, mitred at 45 degrees at the corners
host_interface: column tops or leg dowels at the corners
joint_schedule: mitre, reinforced internally (block or leg dowel - not resolvable)
surface_realization: relief on the long faces, painted row on the short faces
permitted_variation: rail height; plan aspect; ornament assignment PER FACE
incompatible_excluded: tenoned rail frames
note: The corner reinforcement is inferred, not seen - see the corresponding unresolved brace row.

construction_invariant: A horizontal rail that separates and carries drawers. Its receiver schedule is what defines it: it tenons into the corner posts AND into the interior partitions, and it takes the drawer runners.
host_interface: corner posts and interior partitions
joint_schedule: tenoned into posts and partitions; receives drawer runners; may carry a lock keeper
assembly_role: divides a drawer stack and carries its load
permitted_variation: length; height; COUNT (drives drawer count); front-edge profile; keeper plate presence
incompatible_excluded: panel-frame stock (spans openings, carries nothing); frieze and plinth rails (no drawer load, different receiver); back rails (secondary wood, no show face)
note: Split out of v3's rail.case_divider, which combined drawer dividers, panel-frame stock, frieze rails, plinth rails, back rails, gate stock and arched rails into one family on the strength of all being horizontal. R216.b (rails above and below the drawers) and R247.d (the single rail above the drawers, restored by the final audit) have a clear drawer-bounding ROLE but unproved receiver schedules - members, not proof.

construction_invariant: Generic frame stock whose job is to SPAN panel openings. It carries no drawer and no applied show programme - the panel count it spans is the parameter.
geometry_generator: extruded rectangular section, grooved on one edge
host_interface: stiles and muntins of the same frame
joint_schedule: tenoned into stiles; grooved to capture the panel
assembly_role: horizontal member of a frame-and-panel assembly
permitted_variation: length; width; how many panel openings the rail spans; peg pattern
incompatible_excluded: drawer dividers (carry load, different receiver); frieze/plinth rails

construction_invariant: The upper rail of a case front, under the cornice. Carries the show programme and may be arched on its lower edge.
geometry_generator: extruded section, lower edge straight, arched or scalloped
host_interface: corner posts or stiles
joint_schedule: tenoned into posts; the cornice sits on it
assembly_role: top rail of a case front
permitted_variation: span; depth; straight vs arched vs scalloped lower edge
incompatible_excluded: drawer dividers; plinth rails at the base; back rails
note: R216 was split by role in the final patch; only its arched frieze rails (.a) belong here. The drawer-bounding rails went to rail.drawer_divider and the centre-section rails to the AUDIT_ONLY bucket - assigning the aggregate here claimed a frieze role for rails the source distinguishes.

construction_invariant: The base rail of a case, carrying the reeded band and the load down to the feet.
host_interface: corner posts; feet or plinth blocks below
joint_schedule: tenoned into posts; transfers load to the feet
permitted_variation: span; depth; band reed count
incompatible_excluded: frieze rails at the top of the same case - different load path and different treatment

construction_invariant: A plain secondary-wood rail closing the back. No show face, cheaper stock, deliberately undecorated.
host_interface: case sides
joint_schedule: tenoned or nailed
assembly_role: closes the back of a case
permitted_variation: span; depth
incompatible_excluded: any show-face rail

construction_invariant: The fixed frame rails of a table - end rails and long side rails, optionally pierced for a drawer opening.
geometry_generator: extruded section, straight or shaped lower edge
host_interface: corner legs
joint_schedule: tenoned into the legs
surface_realization: primary wood on show faces, secondary behind
permitted_variation: length; depth; pierced for a drawer or not; primary vs secondary wood; straight vs shaped lower edge
incompatible_excluded: case drawer dividers; swinging gate stock
note: AUDIT_ONLY per the final audit - the tenon claim is asserted from type; no joint is visible in the published views.

construction_invariant: The front rails of a chest, where the UPPER rail is deepened to take the lock.
geometry_generator: extruded section, upper deeper than lower
host_interface: corner stiles
joint_schedule: tenoned into the stiles; the upper rail is mortised for a lock
permitted_variation: upper (lock) rail depth vs lower rail depth; run length; straight vs curved lower edge
incompatible_excluded: drawer dividers; frieze rails
note: AUDIT_ONLY per the final audit - the lock mortise and stile tenons are inferred from the rail depths, not seen.

construction_invariant: One stock section serving several roles on one object, distinguished only by which inlay path is run on it. The reusable fact is the STOCK, not the role.
geometry_generator: one extruded section, several path programmes
host_interface: posts or stiles at each end
joint_schedule: tenoned
assembly_role: capital under-rail and drawer bottom rail on the same object
permitted_variation: length; height; which inlay path is applied
incompatible_excluded: rails whose section is driven by a load they carry
note: 'the capital under-rail is the same stock as the drawer bottom rail with a different inlay path' - stated outright.

construction_invariant: A rail recorded as possibly grooved, possibly rebated, possibly mortised - three different receiver schedules, none of them settled.
host_interface: UNRESOLVED
joint_schedule: UNRESOLVED
permitted_variation: length; height; and the open question of which receiver schedule applies
incompatible_excluded: every rail whose schedule IS known
note: AUDIT_ONLY. R379 lists three mutually exclusive schedules ('whether grooved for panels, rebated for bottom boards, or mortised for a lock') and settles none. R216.c - the top and bottom rails of the centre section - records a position but no receiver schedule at all.

construction_invariant: Top and bottom rails bounding an upholstered back opening between the rear posts.
geometry_generator: extruded section; the top rail may be widened to carry a carved frieze
host_interface: rear posts at each end
joint_schedule: tenoned into the rear posts
surface_realization: carved frieze on the front face of the top rail; plain behind
permitted_variation: opening height; bay count; frieze repeat count
incompatible_excluded: seat rails; crest boards sawn to a silhouette
note: 'the same rail with the ornament stripped is a plain crest rail' - ornament is a separable layer on this member.

construction_invariant: A rail existing PURELY as a tacking ground for a cover. No show face, no structural span claim - add more as the back gets taller.
geometry_generator: extruded plain section, lapped past the post
host_interface: back frame posts
joint_schedule: lapped past the central back post
assembly_role: tacking ground for the inside-back cover
permitted_variation: length; height on the back frame; count
incompatible_excluded: structural back-frame rails

construction_invariant: A rail BOWED IN PLAN and serpentine in elevation, sawn from a wide board. Its structural core is bare; all ornament is applied to the outer face.
geometry_generator: sawn from a wide board along two curves (plan bow + elevation serpentine)
host_interface: posts at each end
joint_schedule: OUT OF SCOPE - the end interface is unevidenced and is NOT part of this recipe; a consumer must supply its own end joint
assembly_role: long side rail of a bed
surface_realization: gilt ornament applied to the outer face only; core left bare
permitted_variation: length; bow radius in plan; serpentine sag depth at mid-span
incompatible_excluded: straight rails - a straight member cannot be stretched into this and the stock width requirement is completely different
note: GEOMETRY-ONLY per the final audit. R338.a proves the curved SAWN FORM - bowed in plan, serpentine in elevation, sawn from wide stock - and nothing about the end joint. 'Knockdown or fixed' was removed as a variation axis: it is not a parameter of this recipe, it is an unevidenced fact about a different contract (R338.b, quarantined). What this family delivers is the curve; the interface is external.

construction_invariant: A straight rail whose FINISH is switched by visibility: the same member is plain unfinished wood at the unseen end and fully decorated at the seen end.
host_interface: posts at each end
joint_schedule: tenoned post to post
assembly_role: closes the base of an end frame; rear rail of a case
surface_realization: plain unfinished OR full gilt apron - a switch, not a different part
permitted_variation: length; finished-vs-plain treatment as a visibility-driven flag
incompatible_excluded: curved sawn rails
note: 1954.151 proves it on ONE object: head-end version plain on both faces, foot-end version carries the full gilt apron. Same rail, one boolean.

construction_invariant: A gallery base rail MORTISED at pitch to receive spindles. The mortise pitch is the interface and no other gallery rail has it.
geometry_generator: extruded section with a mortise array
host_interface: posts or frame at each end
joint_schedule: mortise array at fixed pitch for spindle tenons
permitted_variation: length; MORTISE PITCH (drives spindle count)
incompatible_excluded: gallery cap rails and inlaid band rails - neither carries a mortise array
note: Per the audit: gallery base, cap and top rails are split because their interface schedules are NOT proven equivalent. This one's schedule is a mortise array.

construction_invariant: The rail capping a gallery. Receives spindle tops; its own face may carry a bead run.
geometry_generator: extruded section, optionally with a bead run
host_interface: spindle tops below
joint_schedule: receives spindle tenons from below
surface_realization: bead run on the face, or plain
permitted_variation: length; profile depth; whether it carries a bead run
incompatible_excluded: the mortised base rail; inlaid band rails

construction_invariant: A rail whose defining feature is a stretchable inlaid band with FIXED-WIDTH terminal cells - a two-part layout that generalises to any long band.
geometry_generator: extruded section; the inlay is a separate path stretched to the rail length
host_interface: posts or frame at each end
joint_schedule: tenoned
assembly_role: show rail of a headboard/footboard or bed side
surface_realization: marquetry band: fixed terminal cells + stretchable centre
permitted_variation: length; moulding member count on the edges; whether the centre medallion is present
incompatible_excluded: gallery rails with spindle interfaces
note: 'the centre ribbon-knot is a fixed medallion with a stretchable scroll to either side' - a genuinely reusable layout rule.

construction_invariant: A reeded CYLINDRICAL rod running fore-aft with a carved terminal. A solid of revolution with a swept reed - not a sawn board.
geometry_generator: revolve + reed sweep; carved terminal master at the front
host_interface: arm post below at the front; rear post behind
joint_schedule: dies into a carved bracket at the rear post
surface_realization: reeded, gilt; ram's-head/lion-head/volute terminal as a swappable master
permitted_variation: length; reed count; terminal master choice
incompatible_excluded: flat swept arm boards - a board and a rod share only the centre path
note: Per the audit: split from flat swept-board arms unless only the centre-path vocabulary is shared. Here only the centre path is shared.

construction_invariant: One sawn, COMPOUND-CURVED board doing the whole arm, terminating in a cyma scroll. Mirror-symmetric pair from one profile.
geometry_generator: sawn board along a compound curve; cyma scroll at the terminal
host_interface: arm posts below; back frame behind
joint_schedule: lapped or tenoned onto the arm posts
permitted_variation: scroll tightness; flare angle; board thickness; arm height above seat
incompatible_excluded: round reeded rods

construction_invariant: An arm rail whose length drives ARCH COUNT in lockstep with spindle count - the arcade is a composition rule, not a single member.
host_interface: seat rail below via posts
joint_schedule: spindles tenon between seat rail and arm rail
surface_realization: gilt; top face padded or bare
permitted_variation: length -> arch count (5 arches over 4 spindles + 1 post here); arch springing height; whether the top face is padded
incompatible_excluded: single-member arms
note: 'the single most transplantable assembly on the object.'

construction_invariant: A MOVING assembly: swing rail + pivot + swing leg + a stop that is not resolvable. It is one mechanism and must be authored as one, with the stop left open.
geometry_generator: rail + pivot joint + leg, with a motion range
host_interface: rear rail of the carcase
joint_schedule: PIVOT (knuckle or pin) at the inboard end; the leg is a standard leg blank with an extended UNFINISHED upper post because it is concealed when closed
assembly_role: supports a drop leaf when open; nests against the rear rail when closed
surface_realization: show wood on the leg; raw saw-marked concealed extension
permitted_variation: swing length; pivot offset from the rail end; leg blank parameters; concealed-extension length
incompatible_excluded: static rails and static legs
note: v3 marked R147 BOTH proven and unresolved - the fail-closed check in v3.1 caught it. The rail and its pivot ARE visible (alt7 shows it extended at 90 degrees carrying the swing leg); what is unresolved is the STOP, which has no BOM row of its own and is therefore recorded here as a family-level open question rather than as a penalty on a row that is actually well evidenced. Per the audit, authored as rail + pivot + support + UNRESOLVED STOP. No view resolves what limits the swing at 90 degrees. The 'concealed extension' parameter generalises to any moving member.

construction_invariant: A flat board rail that SWINGS with a gate and carries pins along its face.
geometry_generator: flat board with shaped pivot end and a pin array
host_interface: gate post pivot
joint_schedule: pivot at one end; pins along the face
assembly_role: upper member of a swinging gate
permitted_variation: length (sets how far under the leaf the gate reaches); thickness; pivot-end shaping; pin count
incompatible_excluded: fixed frame rails

construction_invariant: A triangular or quarter block glued into an inside frame corner. ONLY rows where a block was actually seen are members.
geometry_generator: prism, two mating faces cut to the frame angle
host_interface: two inside rail faces at a corner
joint_schedule: glued; one instance mates to a CURVED end apron, so the recipe needs a 'seat against a swept surface' parameter
surface_realization: none - never seen in the finished object
permitted_variation: block section; leg length; chamfer; flat-vs-swept mating face
incompatible_excluded: every INFERRED block (47, 53, 139, 241) - they carry zero weight and may not establish this family's joint; the case-base locator, which does a different job
note: Per the audit, exactly the two EVIDENCED rows. v2 carried 7 members of which 4 were inferred; this was the single worst evidence dilution in v2.

construction_invariant: A block at the base corners that LOCATES a case sitting loose on top. It positions, it does not stiffen.
host_interface: base top surface; the loose case above
joint_schedule: glued to the base; the case above simply sits within them
permitted_variation: block length and angle
incompatible_excluded: corner glue blocks, which reinforce a joint rather than locate a separate case
note: Moved out of the glue-block family per the audit: 'these sit at the base corners and appear to locate the case that sits loose on top.'

construction_invariant: A brass quadrant stay / lopper arm limiting a fall front. Visible, metal, and its upper end slides in a slot.
host_interface: carcass stile (slot) and fall front (fixed end)
joint_schedule: slides in a slot in the carcass stile, or is pinned
assembly_role: limits and supports a falling front
permitted_variation: arc radius and chord length (set by fall depth); strap width; sliding vs pinned upper end
incompatible_excluded: unseen axial tie rods - opposite evidence status and opposite construction
note: Per the audit: visible quadrant metal stays split from unseen axial tie rods.

construction_invariant: A shaped sawn bracket/console whose 2D profile is swept to a constant thickness. One curve asset, several length settings.
geometry_generator: 2D cyma/ogee profile swept to constant thickness
host_interface: post and the member it braces
joint_schedule: let in, screwed, or pegged; 1954.151 adds a let-in iron keeper plate
assembly_role: ties a crest or canopy down to a post; gusset between arm rail and stile
surface_realization: gilt or matched to the frame; may be pierced
permitted_variation: arc radius; span; rise; thickness; hole count and position; piercing radius
incompatible_excluded: glue blocks (unseen, structural-only)
note: 'The same curve appears again at the headboard ends, so it is ONE curve asset with two length settings.'

construction_invariant: An end cleat battened across a lid underside to resist cupping. Fixing type doubles as an age/repair storytelling axis.
host_interface: lid underside
joint_schedule: pegged, nailed or screwed - the choice is the period/repair signal
surface_realization: may be moulded to match the lid edge; or pale unpatinated modern wood
permitted_variation: cleat width; taper of the chamfered ends; fixing pattern
incompatible_excluded: structural frame braces
note: 1971.281's cleats are explicitly a LATER REPAIR in pale unpatinated wood with modern slotted screws - a ready-made 'this has been repaired' variant.

construction_invariant: A flat plate laid over a failed joint and pegged at its corners - a shop-level repair, not original construction.
geometry_generator: flat rectangular plate with a peg array
host_interface: outside face of a rail over a leg tenon
joint_schedule: four round pegs at the corners
surface_realization: bare wood, contrasting with the finished frame
permitted_variation: plate outline; peg count and pattern
incompatible_excluded: original structural members
note: 'Extremely valuable as a this-frame-has-been-repaired decal for aged furniture variants.'

construction_invariant: An internal grid inside a seat rectangle: one longitudinal member crossed by front-to-back sticks. Spacing is a function of seat length.
geometry_generator: longitudinal member + crossing sticks, some straight and some sawn to a shallow arc
host_interface: inside faces of the seat rails
joint_schedule: lapped over or tenoned into the rails
assembly_role: supports the seat platform over a long span
permitted_variation: brace spacing/count as a function of seat length; straight vs arced stick; lapped vs tenoned
incompatible_excluded: corner blocks

construction_invariant: Structural joinery: stiles + rails + muntins, grooved to CAPTURE a floating panel. The grammar is the asset, not any one frame.
host_interface: carcase or door opening
joint_schedule: mortise-and-tenon, often PEGGED; panels float in grooves, never glued
assembly_role: structural side, back or door of a case
surface_realization: moulded lip on the inner edge; may receive applied ornament
permitted_variation: bay count; bay aspect ratio; stile/rail widths; groove depth; muntin count
incompatible_excluded: applied moulded surrounds, which are trim on a board and hold nothing; the unresolved 69.140ab case sides
note: 'the grammar (stiles + rails + muntins + captured panels) is the reusable object, not the specific frame.'

construction_invariant: Applied trim MITRED around an aperture on a board. It captures nothing and carries no load - the opposite construction to a joined frame.
geometry_generator: moulded profile mitred into a closed loop
host_interface: the face of a board or carcase front
joint_schedule: MITRE at the corners; glued to the ground
permitted_variation: aperture size; number of concentric steps; reed pitch; step count in the profile stack
incompatible_excluded: structural stile-rail-muntin grids
note: Kept separate from the joined grid per the audit, membership corrected. The mitre is the discriminator: joined frames tenon, applied surrounds mitre.

construction_invariant: A four-sided enclosure made of rail / rail / bracket / bracket around a pierced field - NOT a stile-and-rail frame and not applied trim.
geometry_generator: two horizontal rails closed at each end by a shaped bracket
host_interface: arm assembly of a chair
joint_schedule: rails tenon to the brackets; the pierced field is captured between
assembly_role: encloses a pierced lattice field under an arm
permitted_variation: field length; field height; bracket master; lattice cell count
incompatible_excluded: both frame families - it has no stiles and no mitred trim
note: Created per the audit as its own enclosure for FC-01-2012_216. The source calls it 'the single most transferable assembly rule on the object'.

construction_invariant: A wooden board floating free in the surrounding frame's grooves - never glued, so it can move. The BLANK is separable from whatever is done to its face.
host_interface: grooves of the surrounding frame
joint_schedule: floats in the groove; NO glue - that is the defining constraint
surface_realization: plain, carved, marquetried, fielded or glazed - all are face programs on one blank
permitted_variation: aspect ratio; thickness; bevel/fielding depth; rectangular vs shouldered field; face program
incompatible_excluded: upholstered fields, which are a padded volume with no groove interface
note: REPAIRED TWICE. v3 admitted 11 members on asserted grooves; v3.1 kept four; the final audit cut two more. Only TWO rows prove the exact groove/captured-panel contract: R363 GROOVE STATED ('a plain, a carved, and a pierced variant all share one GROOVE-SET blank') and R198, whose companion R197 records the full grammar WITH groove depth ('stiles + rails + muntins + captured panels', 'groove depth'). R273 and R381 are quarantined as frame_layout_only: their companions (R272, R380) prove frame layout, panel count and peg pattern - never the concealed capture. Weighted evidence 10.0 -> 4.0 -> 2.0 across the three passes. Each drop is a correction.

construction_invariant: A padded volume dropped into a frame rebate. Same SLOT as a wooden panel, entirely different construction - no groove, no wood movement, a crown instead of a thickness.
geometry_generator: padded volume with a crowned surface
host_interface: frame rebate; tacked to the frame or to webbing
joint_schedule: tacked, not captured - there is no groove
assembly_role: fills a frame opening with textile
permitted_variation: field crown/loft; edge radius; cover material
incompatible_excluded: wooden floating panels
note: Preserved from v2 - the audit confirms this distinction was correct. 'a clean demonstration that the frame and the field are separable slots.'

construction_invariant: A cornice built as a STACK of swept profile members, mitred at the corners and returning on the visible sides.
geometry_generator: stacked swept profiles along a rectangular path
host_interface: top of a case or tester
joint_schedule: mitred returns at the corners; dies into the posts
surface_realization: fillet/cove/ogee stack, optionally with a dentil course
permitted_variation: stack depth; fillet count; projection; whether it returns on the sides only or wraps; dentil pitch
incompatible_excluded: shaped sawn crest boards, which are a silhouette cut from a board, not a swept stack
note: Preserved from v2; the audit confirms stacked cornice vs shaped sawn crest is a real distinction.

construction_invariant: A single board SAWN to a silhouette, carved on the front face only. The rear proves it: a plain sawn board with a screw and peg line.
geometry_generator: 2D silhouette curve cut from a board
host_interface: top rail of the back or case
joint_schedule: screwed and pegged to the top rail
assembly_role: crowns a chair back or case front
surface_realization: relief carving on the FRONT ONLY
permitted_variation: pitch/span; lobe count (scales with seat count); lobe amplitude; end sweep; relief content
incompatible_excluded: stacked cornice runs; laminated curved crests
note: 'the rear views prove the back face is a plain sawn board with a screw and peg line where it fixes to the top rail.' The top-edge curve is the transferable asset.

construction_invariant: An arched crest BUILT UP from laminated curved segments - lamination lines are visible. It cannot be cut from one board, which is the whole point.
geometry_generator: laminated curved segments following an arc
host_interface: post caps at each end
joint_schedule: stepped down through an ogee shoulder to the post cap
assembly_role: arched cresting of a bed end
permitted_variation: arch span; arch rise; shoulder step height; garland density
incompatible_excluded: single-board sawn crests - the stock requirement is completely different
note: Split from the sawn-board family on construction: 'built up from laminated curved segments (lamination lines visible in alt9/alt10/alt11)'.

construction_invariant: A crest that ROLLS backward over the top of the back and terminates in a carved spiral at each corner - a swept roll, not a flat silhouette.
geometry_generator: swept roll section along the back's top curve, with a carved volute terminal master
host_interface: top of the back frame
joint_schedule: continuous with the back frame stiles
permitted_variation: roll radius; spiral tightness at each end
incompatible_excluded: flat sawn crest boards

construction_invariant: A moulded top rail bent to a flattened D-curve in plan, with ASYMMETRIC ornament: plain outside, decorated inside.
geometry_generator: moulded section swept along a flattened D-curve
host_interface: back frame stiles
joint_schedule: continuous with the stiles
assembly_role: wraps and crowns a barrel-plan back
surface_realization: plain outside face; reeded and disc-inlaid inside face
permitted_variation: corner radius; crown height; arc width; the outside/inside ornament asymmetry
incompatible_excluded: sawn silhouette crests
note: The inside/outside asymmetry rule is itself reusable and is recorded as a variation axis rather than a separate family.

construction_invariant: A metal capital that is itself a small assembly grammar - a bell plus swap-in ornament slots - explicitly 'not one blob'.
geometry_generator: bell profile + corner volute masses + central mask slot + cresting slot
host_interface: top of the shaft; abacus above
joint_schedule: seated/threaded on the shaft
surface_realization: gilt brass, fluted/reeded bell, cabled torus
permitted_variation: bell profile; which ornament fills each slot; volute mass scale
incompatible_excluded: wooden carved capitals

construction_invariant: NOT one moulding asset. A PROFILING TOOLKIT: a library of profile atoms, the stacks built from them, the paths they sweep along, and the rules for mitres, stopped ends and junctions. Objects state repeatedly that ONE section serves several roles at several scales, which is what makes this a capability rather than a part.
geometry_generator: sweep of a 2D section along an arbitrary path; sections stack
host_interface: any edge, aperture or run on any object
joint_schedule: mitre at corners; stopped ends; dies into posts; returns on visible faces
surface_realization: the section IS the surface event
permitted_variation: PROFILE ATOMS (observed: fillet, ovolo, cavetto, ogee, astragal/bead, thumbnail, chamfer, reed, flute, bolection); STACK depth and member count; PATH (straight, rectangular loop, serpentine, arc); MITRE vs STOPPED END; junction/return rule; scale
incompatible_excluded: repeated-cell runs, where a discrete cell is instanced rather than a section swept - that is a different generator
note: Re-described as a toolkit per the audit. The corpus states the reuse explicitly: 'one profile serves drawer surrounds, side-panel frames and the plinth at different scales' (69.146.2); 'the same few sections repeat as door-panel bolection, pilaster cross-blocks, base cap, and base plinth' (2019.59); 'Sectioning the profiles once and sweeping them along arbitrary rectangles covers essentially all of this object's linear detail' (69.146.3).

construction_invariant: A discrete carved or cast CELL instanced along a path at a pitch. The generator is instancing, not sweeping - a constant-section sweep cannot produce it.
geometry_generator: instance a cell master along a path at a pitch
host_interface: any edge or drum
joint_schedule: carved integral or applied as a sleeve
permitted_variation: run length; cell pitch; cell master choice; instance count around a circumference
incompatible_excluded: constant-profile sweeps
note: Preserved from v2 - the audit confirms constant-profile sweep vs repeated-cell run is a real distinction. 2002.298.1 gives the strongest exact-reuse evidence in the whole corpus: 'The upper and lower sleeves are the SAME part used twice.'

construction_invariant: A plain revolved ring clamping the edge of a band or sleeve. One shape, one parameter.
host_interface: drum rims and band edges
joint_schedule: clamped/seated on the drum
assembly_role: closes a joint between stacked drums
permitted_variation: diameter
incompatible_excluded: swept runs along open paths
note: 'At least 8 are visible, but individual rings merge visually with the adjacent drum rims at every published resolution, so NO HONEST COUNT EXISTS.'

construction_invariant: A reeded collar cut IN THE STONE itself, with no metal ring at all. It proves the jewel bands are not all metal, so it is a construction fact as well as a part.
geometry_generator: reeds cut into the stone drum
host_interface: the shaft itself - subtractive, not applied
joint_schedule: none - it is the shaft
permitted_variation: reed count; register depth
incompatible_excluded: applied gilt collars - opposite construction (subtractive vs applied)
note: 'Important construction fact: it proves the jewel bands are not all metal.'

construction_invariant: The PLACEMENT AND INSTANCING SYSTEM ONLY - path pitch, ring array, mirroring and graded scatter. It owns no geometry. Every actual relief master is its own part identity in the relief.* families generated below.
geometry_generator: a placement rule applied to a master supplied from elsewhere
host_interface: any show face
joint_schedule: n/a - the hosted master carries its own interface
assembly_role: distributes masters over a surface or run
surface_realization: n/a - the master carries the surface
permitted_variation: path pitch; ring count; instance scale ramp along a run; mirroring; GRADED FALL (dense at the top, thinning downward, lower third empty on tall panels - 69.140ab)
incompatible_excluded: all relief geometry - v3 merged 17 unrelated masters into this family purely because they all use transforms, which is not a shared construction
note: REBUILT in v3.1. v3's ornament.instanced_relief_master held 17 members and was the assembly-lane leader at score 22.59 on the strength of an argument that amounts to 'these all get placed somewhere'. The three members kept here are the rows that actually record a PLACEMENT RULE as the reusable thing (paterae counted per rail face; palmettes at a measured ~71px pitch; blocks swapped within one layout slot). Everything else moved to its own master.

construction_invariant: A separately carved garland SCREWED to a plain sawn backing. The interface is proved by a photograph of the back - the clearest applied-ornament evidence in the corpus.
geometry_generator: carved swag master, hung along a path
host_interface: a plain sawn backing board
joint_schedule: SCREWED - seen from behind in alt6
permitted_variation: swag length; sag depth; flower density; hung as a drop, a spiral or a continuous run
incompatible_excluded: ornament carved integral to its ground
note: 'alt6 shows one from behind: a separately carved element SCREWED to a plain sawn backing, which is exactly the applied-ornament workflow to copy.'

construction_invariant: Ornament cut INTO the parent member's own face. There is no separate part and no interface - modelling it as an applied master is the error.
geometry_generator: subtractive carving on the parent face
host_interface: the parent member itself
joint_schedule: none - it is the parent
assembly_role: surface enrichment integral to a panel or block
permitted_variation: fold width; fold count per panel; terminal motif; bead pitch; density from austere 2-fold to crowded 5-fold
incompatible_excluded: applied masters with a glue or screw interface
note: v3 merged three incompatible things here. R303.a is an APPLIED carved wreath (glued on, not cut into the host) and R303.b is an INSET MARQUETRY CELL (a veneer cut, not geometry at all). Both are now their own families. Only R364's linenfold is actually carved into the host face.

construction_invariant: A small SET of flat masters (blossom, leaf, stem) re-scattered to fill any field. Retargeting is by re-scattering, never by new art.
geometry_generator: flat 2D masters placed by a scatter rule with rotation and scale jitter
host_interface: a veneered field
joint_schedule: let into the veneer - a surface program, not a solid
assembly_role: fills a panel or band with pattern
surface_realization: contrasting veneers, engraved detail, dot accents
permitted_variation: instance rotation, scale and packing density; GRADED FALL (dense at top, thinning downward); field aspect ratio
incompatible_excluded: carved relief masters, which are solids
note: NARROWED in v3.1 to genuine reusable BOTANICAL motif sets. Removed: R154 (pure closed line-figures, no botanical master at all - the row says so), R186 (a keyhole cartouche, a functional marker not a field filler), and R114 (mixed - split into a veneer-cut star and a host-carved boss, which cannot share a recipe). 69.140ab records a placement rule worth having: 'every field is a graded fall - dense at the top, thinning downward, with the lower third left empty on the tall door and side panels, while the short drawer and frieze bands run at even high density throughout.'

construction_invariant: A carved lion/grotesque head, hand-authored, instanced mirror-left and mirror-right.
host_interface: arm terminal or knee
joint_schedule: carved integral or applied
permitted_variation: scale; mirror only
incompatible_excluded: every other figural master - they are unrelated sculptures, not one family

construction_invariant: A classicising female head with fillet headdress and pendant collar on a capital face.
host_interface: capital face
joint_schedule: cast integral with the capital
permitted_variation: scale only
incompatible_excluded: the leonine corner mask on the SAME capital - a different sculpture
note: 'Every published view is the same frontal aspect, so only ONE mask has ever been seen; the square abacus implies four, one per face, but that is not observed.'

construction_invariant: A maned leonine/grotesque head at a capital corner, terminating in a scroll volute.
host_interface: capital corner
joint_schedule: cast integral with the capital
permitted_variation: scale only
incompatible_excluded: the female mask on the same capital
note: 'Two are visible on the one photographed face; four corners are implied but not seen.'

construction_invariant: A winged sun disk with flanking uraei - drops unchanged onto any long horizontal ground.
geometry_generator: hand-authored sculpture with a span parameter
host_interface: a long horizontal ground
joint_schedule: UNRESOLVED - carved integral to the rail or applied is not stated
permitted_variation: wingspan scales to rail length; feather-row count; disk diameter
incompatible_excluded: the lotus rows and petal capitals on the same object
note: 'the single highest-value donor element in the object' - but its interface is explicitly unresolved, so it cannot be admitted as a donor on that claim.

construction_invariant: An overlapping lotus-petal bell capital. The petal profile is the generative unit and could be re-swept onto vase turnings and urn bases.
geometry_generator: one petal master arrayed radially around the capital bell
host_interface: column head
joint_schedule: bell/host attachment UNRESOLVED - the petal geometry on the bell is visible; how the bell meets the column is not evidenced
permitted_variation: petal count around the bell; petal length relative to bell height; tip sharpness
incompatible_excluded: the winged sun disk and painted lotus rows
note: Reclassified from bespoke_hero in v3.1: ONE petal master arrayed radially around a bell is a recipe, not a hero carving - 'The same petal profile is the generative unit for the capital and could be re-swept onto vase turnings, urn bases, or column feet.' Final-audit corrections: the petals are NOT claimed carved integral to the column (attachment unresolved -> construction uncertainty), and the unseen total petal count ('petals wrap the bell; only the near faces are visible') is QUANTITY doubt only - recorded here rather than as a penalty.

construction_invariant: A fluted, footed inlaid urn used as a composition anchor at panel centres.
host_interface: a veneered panel centre
joint_schedule: let into the veneer
permitted_variation: scale only - it is a signature mark, not a kit part
incompatible_excluded: the arcade master on the same object; the blossom motif sets

construction_invariant: A low colonnaded arcade on a plinth, used in place of a keyhole on the bottom drawer.
host_interface: a drawer front
joint_schedule: let into the veneer
permitted_variation: scale only
incompatible_excluded: the urn master on the same object
note: Split from the urn per the audit: 'Split unrelated figural carvings into individual bespoke masters.' The source itself calls them two one-off masters.

construction_invariant: A central carved palmette cartouche with fluted crown and four flanking S-scroll tendrils.
host_interface: centre of an arm lattice
joint_schedule: applied
permitted_variation: cartouche height; tendril count and curvature
incompatible_excluded: the disc-in-bezel master it sits among
note: 'Directly seen on one arm only; the second is asserted from the object's bilateral symmetry, not observed.'

construction_invariant: A let-in line of contrasting wood following an OFFSET of the silhouette of the face it sits on. It is an offset-inset generator, not drawn art.
geometry_generator: offset-inset of a face silhouette, swept at a constant line width
host_interface: a veneered or solid show face
joint_schedule: LET IN - a groove cut and filled, so it is real geometry
permitted_variation: line width; inset distance from the part edge; corner radius; path outline (plain rectangle vs cusped cartouche); PATH CURVATURE (bent around ogee braces on 69.146.1); pass count per face - rear faces get zero, show faces one to two
incompatible_excluded: painted line-work, which cuts no geometry; engraved-and-filled stone lines
note: 1969.262 states the generator: 'Every figure here is a single-width light line offsetting the silhouette of the face it sits on - an offset-inset generator, not drawn art.'

construction_invariant: The SAME path vocabulary executed in paint or gilding. No groove, no let-in element - the geometry is untouched and only the shader differs.
geometry_generator: the same path generator, resolved to a texture rather than geometry
host_interface: a painted or gilt ground
joint_schedule: NONE - it is a surface treatment
surface_realization: painted line, zigzag, dot banding, gilt striping
permitted_variation: line weight; colour pair; zigzag amplitude and wavelength; stripe width and gap
incompatible_excluded: let-in stringing, which is geometry
note: Split from let-in stringing on construction, not on appearance. The sources themselves flag the shared vocabulary: 'the path generator is shared and only the surface shader differs.' Only the centre-path vocabulary is shared, which is exactly the audit's stated test.

construction_invariant: Line ornament CUT INTO STONE and filled with pigment - subtractive on a mineral ground.
geometry_generator: engraved groove following a path, pigment-filled
host_interface: polished alabaster
joint_schedule: incised and filled
permitted_variation: register count; motif per register; wrap circumference
incompatible_excluded: wood stringing and painted line-work
note: 'At least 4 distinct registers, but each wraps 360 degrees and only ~half is ever visible' - the count is bounded below only.

construction_invariant: A discrete cell used as PUNCTUATION wherever a linear path turns a corner or terminates. It is a placement rule as much as a shape.
geometry_generator: a cell master + a rule keyed to path corners and terminations
host_interface: the ends and corners of an inlay path
joint_schedule: let in with the path
permitted_variation: cell size; spacing pitch along the run; the corner/termination rule itself
incompatible_excluded: the continuous line the cells punctuate
note: 'It is the punctuation mark used wherever a linear path turns a corner or terminates - a PLACEMENT RULE as much as a shape.'

construction_invariant: A row of discrete inlaid cells at a pitch - instancing, not a continuous line.
